question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=-4x+2?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4x+2 \\  & =-4(0)+2 \\  & =0+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,2).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=-2.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4x+2 \\  & =-4(-2)+2 \\  & =8+2 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(-2,10).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=-4x+2.$
